ecsOverview.text: E-commerce Is Borderless. Its Obligations Are Not.
ecsOverview.body: Selling online makes international expansion more accessible, but operating across multiple markets introduces significant financial, tax and regulatory responsibilities.

rightColumn.text: From marketplace sellers and direct-to-consumer brands to established international retailers, businesses need reliable financial information, appropriate structures and a clear understanding of their obligations in each jurisdiction.

ecsRevenue.title: Revenue Is Only Part of the Picture.
ecsRevenue.conclusion: Strong online sales do not necessarily translate into financial strength. Understanding the relationship between revenue, margins, obligations and cash flow is essential to building a resilient e-commerce business.

items.text: Sales growth can conceal declining margins. Platform fees, fulfilment costs, refunds and advertising expenditure directly affect profitability.
International sales create local obligations. Tax registrations, reporting requirements and customs arrangements depend on where business activities take place.
Inventory can restrict working capital. Stock purchases and fulfilment arrangements can absorb cash before revenue is received.
Reliable reporting supports better decisions. Accurate financial information helps management assess performance, investment requirements and expansion opportunities.

ecsInventory.title: Inventory Is More Than Stock. It Is Capital Already Committed.
ecsInventory.lead: For many e-commerce businesses, inventory represents a significant financial commitment.

cards.text: Inventory Management: Understanding inventory valuation, cost allocation and reporting requirements across locations.
Cash-Flow Planning: Forecasting stock purchases, supplier payments and financing needs to support continued operations.

ecsInventory.body: Purchasing decisions, international storage, fulfilment arrangements and changing customer demand can create substantial working-capital pressure.
ecsInventory.statement: Reliable financial information helps management understand how inventory decisions affect profitability, liquidity and future growth.

ecsChannels.lead: E-commerce businesses operate through different sales, fulfilment and distribution structures.
ecsChannels.leadStrong: Each model creates its own accounting, taxation and financial management requirements.

ecsQuestions.title: The Questions E-commerce Businesses Are Asking.

items.question: Where do we have tax obligations?
items.answer: Sales destinations, inventory locations, business activities and applicable registration requirements.

items.question: Are our reported margins accurate?
items.answer: Marketplace fees, refunds, fulfilment costs, currency movements and financial reconciliations.

items.question: Is our international structure appropriate?
items.answer: Corporate entities, tax exposure, intercompany transactions and governance requirements.

items.question: How much working capital do we need?
items.answer: Inventory commitments, supplier payments, tax liabilities and forecast cash requirements.

items.question: Are we ready for external investment?
items.answer: Reporting quality, financial controls, ownership structures and due diligence readiness.

items.question: Can our financial infrastructure support growth?
items.answer: Accounting systems, reporting capacity, internal controls and international coordination.
